blocks.text: Origin / creation. Young people, educators, artists, caregivers, and philosophers organized against the demand that a valuable life must be historically unprecedented.
Identity / human status. Artificial Era Zero social coalitions. “Firstless” was first imposed as a stigma and later reclaimed.
Importance. They defended ordinary life, inherited art, repeated care, and personal distinctness from civilizational novelty metrics.

Decline or transformation. Coalitions dispersed across schools, arts, low-model communities, Repetitionist traditions, and decline-era politics. Some branches denied the real collective problem of closure.

Final status / surviving function. No single coalition reached the Reduction. Their central principle remains canon: external novelty is needed for continued transformation, not to make existing lives worthwhile.
